newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yamaichi to buy new shares in ailing unit--source.
newsitem.headline: Yamaichi to buy new shares in ailing unit--source.

text.p: Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd will buy about 600 million yen in new shares of an affiliated brokerage, Daichu Securities Co, to help prop up the troubled unit, a company source said on Wednesday.
The shares are to be issued through a third-party allotment as early as next week.

Separately, a spokesman in Tokyo for Yamaichi, one of Japan's "Big Four" brokerage houses, told Reuters on Wednesday that the company is mulling various options on how to assist its financially troubled affiliates, including Daichu.
But the spokesman stopped short of saying whether Yamaichi would buy any new shares to be issued by Daichu and Ogawa Shoken, two small brokerages based in Osaka.

Earlier, another Yamaichi spokesman said one option for helping its affiliated brokerages, including Daichu and Ogawa, would be to merge them into one entity. He said the firm would decide on steps to aid its affiliates as soon as possible.
"The company is considering helping its affiliates from a number of standpoints. A merger is one option," the Yamaichi spokesman told Reuters in Tokyo.
The affiliates also include Naigai Securities Co Ltd, a medium-sized brokerage based in Tokyo, and Naito Securities Co Ltd, a medium-sized brokerage based in Osaka.
Japan's mass-circulation daily Yomiuri Shimbun reported on Wednesday that Yamaichi planned to merge up to four of its affiliated brokerages in order to rescue two of them.
Yamaichi had begun talks on a merger which would involve two troubled Osaka-based affiliates, Daichu and Ogawa, as well as Naigai Securities and possibly Naito Securities, Yomiuri reported.
Daichu, Ogawa and Naito earlier this year each lost several hundred million yen in failed margin transactions and turned to Yamaichi for help, the paper said.
An outline for the merger would be worked out this weekend, but Yamaichi may face opposition from Naigai shareholders such as Nippon Life Insurance Co, Yomiuri said.
